question: In the channelized-intersection example in Figure 2A-3, how far from the nose of the island is the YIELD sign shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (Channelized intersection) of Figure 2A-3, the sign placed on the triangular channelizing island is dimensioned at a minimum of 2 feet from the nose (and side edges) of the island to the sign. This matches the general guidance that signs on raised islands should have at least a 2-foot clearance from the outer edge of the island. (The additional YIELD sign along the right-hand side of the channelized turn lane is shown at the standard 6 ft to 12 ft minimum lateral offset from the roadway edge.) Guidance (recommended): - "Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-3, Drawing B ("Channelized intersection") labels "2 ft MIN." from the nose of the channelizing island to the sign, with a second "2 ft MIN." clearance from the island's side edge, and shows the YIELD sign along the channelized turn roadway at a "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." lateral offset. - [Image 4] The full-page view of Figure 2A-3 confirms the same "2 ft MIN." dimensions at the island nose in Drawing B and the note that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. Citations: - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Section 8A.06 Guidance §3 (p.989) - Page 93
gold_answer: At least 2 feet from the nose of the island.
